info.description:
Welcome to the public API for HydroVu. This page describes the authentication methods
and endpoints required to access your HydroVu data programmatically.

The API exposes endpoints for users to query their available `locations` and associated `readings`.
There is a demo account set up for users to explore this API using the clientId `PublicApiDemo` and the clientSecret `PublicApiSecret`,
however the data is curated for demo purposes only.
Users may also connect to a real account here to explore the API using their own data.

### Authentication

User authentication is handled via [OAuth2 Client Credentials](https://oauth.net/2/grant-types/client-credentials/).
To gain access to an API session, an application must use a client ID and client secret.
Any admin user can log in to HydroVu and create these credentials on the [People and Permissions page](/#/company-dashboard/users/list).
See the FAQ entitled [How do I access the HydroVu API](https://in-situ.com/us/faq/software-help/hydrovu-faqs/how-do-i-access-the-hydrovu-api)
for complete instructions.

The API has a rate-limiting scheme to protect against malicious or abusive use of the system.
A user will be limited to no more than 1000 requests/minute.
The response header `x-isi-requests-this-minute` indicates the number of requests performed since the start of the minute,
and the response header `x-isi-requests-timeout` indicates the time that the next minute will start.

### Paging

Paging is handled through the use of HTTP headers. Responses will have a header `x-isi-next-page` and a header `x-isi-prev-page`
that can be inserted into a request header `x-isi-start-page` to fetch the next or previous page respectively.
If no start page is provided, the first page will be used. If the response does not have a next or previous page,
the headers are not provided.

**NOTE:** All filters must be the same when fetching subsequent pages. Any filter changes will result in the page being invalidated.

get.description: This endpoint can provide you with mappings between the SIS ids or HydroVu keys provided by ot her endpoints, and the information they represent. If a unit or parameter is not recognized by HydroVu, there is no mapping here and is considered a user type.

get.summary: View the list of locations accessible to your account
get.description: This endpoint will return a list of all the locations for your company. Use the `id` property to retrieve further information and data about the location.

This endpoint will provide the data recorded at a location. Select the location by `id`, and then add a query parameter for `startTime`. `startTime` is an integer timestamp in seconds from the start of the Linux epoch (00:00 1st Jan 1970 UTC). The service will find the next block of data that starts at or after your timestamp, and return it. A reading may be a consolidation of multiple readings if the sampling rate is higher than once per minute.

Example: Using an `id` from the locations list, and a `startTime` of 0, you can view the data starting from the first reading on the location. If the data covers multiple pages, the following pages can be retrieved by putting the `x-isi-next-page` response header value into an `x-isi-start-page` request header.

Note: VuLink timestamps are always in UTC. Timestamps from a Cube or Tube may appear in the device's local time.

parameters.description: The data for this locationReadings are listed up to every minute under their parameter. Any minutes with no readings are excluded.

customParameter.description: Indicates whether this is a custom parameter or one defined in the System Integration Specification document

parameterId.description: Matches the parameter Ids defined in the System Integration Specification document -OR- the custom name given to a custom parameter

unitId.description: Matches the unit Ids defined in the System Integration Specification document -OR- the custom unit given to a custom parameter

timestamp.description: Epoch time in seconds when this reading was recorded

value.description: The value of this reading. If there was more than 1 reading in this minute, this value will be the average of all the readings during that minute.
